title: Pumping test 'Oude Korendijk' (Wit 1963), as published in Kruseman & de Ridder (1990/1994), 2nd ed., ILRI Publication 47

source.book: Kruseman, G.P. and de Ridder, N.A., with J.M. Verweij (1994). Analysis and Evaluation of Pumping Test Data, Second Edition (Completely Revised). ILRI Publication 47, Wageningen. ISBN 90 70754 207 (AquaKnow copy: 2000 reprint).
source.dataTable: Table 3.1, p. 59 (piezometers H30 and H90, screen depths 20 m and 24 m)
source.site: p. 56: confined aquifer 18-25 m below surface (KD sought), fully penetrating screen, Q = 9.12 l/s = 788 m3/d for nearly 14 hours; piezometers at 0.8, 30, 90 and 215 m
source.originalData: Wit, K.E. (1963). Report No. 190, Inst. Land and Water Management Research, Wageningen (in Dutch).
source.machineReadableCopy: timflow (MIT), docs/transient/04pumpingtests/data/piezometer_h30.txt and piezometer_h90.txt, https://github.com/timflow-org/timflow (head in m, negative = drawdown; drawdown = -head here)
source.crossCheck: Every time and drawdown value of both files was compared with the text layer of Table 3.1 (p. 59) of the AquaKnow PDF on 2026-11-25: identical.

jacob_H30.method: Jacob (Cooper-Jacob) straight line, Procedure 3.4, graphical fit; validity stated as u < 0.1 for t > 1.4 min

jacob_H90.note: book: less reliable, few points before leakage starts

theis_all.method: Theis type-curve match of s vs t/r2 for H30 and H90 together (H215 discarded); match point W(u) = 1, 1/u = 10, s = 0.16 m, t/r2 = 1.5e-3 min/m2

summary.note: Table 3.3 (p. 71): Thiem 1 385, Thiem 2 390, Theis 392 (S 1.6e-4), Jacob 1 385 (1.7e-4), Jacob 2 370 (4.1e-4), Jacob 3 431 (1.7e-4); Example 3.6 text (p. 70) gives 437 for Jacob 3. Book: late-time data probably influenced by leakage; graphical methods are never accurate (p. 70).
